claim: Expert athletes in interview studies mostly decide by simple pattern match: 60-81% of decisions in Macquet's 2020 review of RPD in sport; diagnosis 13-28%; mental-simulation evaluation 3-24%. Single-athlete and single-team studies sit near this range (handball goalkeeper 46/20/34%, soccer defenders 60/16/23%). The 60-81% range is quoted from one paywalled book chapter (Macquet 2020, CRC Press); the studies and Ns behind it are not named and the mix shifts with time available (rugby, N=16).
agent_test: Log how often the agent needs only a first-match action vs diagnosis vs simulation on a task set; compare accuracy and tokens of forcing match-only against forcing evaluation on every item.
audit_note: All numbers confirmed (Bossard 2022 quoting Macquet 2020: 60-81/13-28/3-24; handball 46/20/34; soccer 60/16/23; rugby N=16 time effect from independent Ashford 2021), but the 60-81% range, the handball and the soccer figures all come from the Bossard/Kermarrec group (Bossard 2022, Le Menn 2019, Kermarrec and Bossard 2014), so the range has one real source.

claim: The simple-match share is not fixed: the goalkeeper's 46% is below the 60% floor of the review, and ranges are wide because coding schemes, roles and sports differ. Rates are coded from retrospective speech, so they are soft.
agent_test: Check coding sensitivity: have two LLM judges code the same agent traces into match/diagnose/simulate and report agreement.
audit_note: Numbers are right (goalkeeper 46% below the 60% floor; wide ranges; retrospective speech), but both sources are from the same Bossard/Kermarrec group and neither says coding schemes, roles and sports are the cause of the spread; that explanation is the researcher's inference.

claim: The '80% first option' figure is about option generation (Take-The-First line, Johnson and Raab 2003), not about the RPD match rate; Bossard 2022 cites it without a named source. It is not interchangeable with the 60-81% RPD range. Re-read 2026-11-19: the Bossard sentence has no in-line citation at all, so the primary source remains unverified; Johnson and Raab 2003 could not be opened.
agent_test: Do not use 80% as a prior. Measure the first-option rate for our agent directly.

claim: First-option choice and less-is-more are mixed: Hepler and Feltz found TTF used on 70% of trials (students, N=72), Raab and Laborde found deliberators less successful in handball (N=54), but Klatt found more options linked to higher accuracy in Brazilian players, and in non-sport tasks option fluency did not predict choice quality (N=141). Partly reconciled: more options raise the best-of-set quality but lower the set mean (Del Missier 2014); Klatt's link is a correlation across players; Raab and Johnson 2007 found equal option counts across expertise with quality differing.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare generating 1, 3 and 5 options before choosing; report accuracy per item difficulty.

claim: Expert visual search differences are task dependent: experts show fewer fixations in some tasks and more in full 11v11 scenes; in Roca 2018 (N=44, extreme groups n=11) more creative players had a higher fixation rate (d=0.91 to 1.32) and found threatening attackers faster (2164 vs 3798 ms). A 2026 meta-analysis of 26 individual-sport studies (N=611) found experts make fewer fixations (SMD -1.52, 95% CI -2.38 to -0.65), so the conflict is task dependence.
agent_test: Compare an agent that scans the whole problem for threats first against one that goes to the obvious item; match tokens.

claim: Coaches' self-estimated intuition share is small and unstable (rugby about 30%, range 5-40%; one adventure coach 90%; N=18); people cannot report it reliably, so usage rates from self-report are weak.
agent_test: Do not trust the agent's own statement of which mode it used; log the mode from the trace.

claim: Video-based decision training in sport shows gains only in small studies (11 players: 55.5 to 61.2% vs 58.7 to 55.0%, interaction p=.002; 4 quarterbacks single-case; baseball r=0.53, p=.052); a 26-article youth review has no pooled effect.
agent_test: Test a case library with outcome notes against none, at equal tokens.

claim: Prompting an LLM with an RPD-style recall-and-simulate frame raised care-seeking accuracy from 63.3% to 67.6% (10 models x 45 vignettes x 10 repeats; re-read in full text 2026-11-19). The gain is almost all in the 13 self-care vignettes (13.4% to 29.8%); nonemergency (30 cases) stayed at about 82% and emergency (2 cases) was 100% to 98%. 88% of errors were over-triage. Data-frame prompt did about as well (66.7%). No gain for GPT-5.2. No length-matched control and no recall-vs-simulate ablation.
agent_test: Replicate with ablation: recall-only, simulate-only, both, plus a length-matched neutral prompt.

claim: On SportQA, GPT-4 (5-shot CoT) scores 85.63 on Level-1 and 78.82 on Level-2 (no human score reported for those levels); on Level-3 humans score 96.63 (easy single-hop), 96.02 (hard single-hop), 94.90 (easy multi-hop) and 91.84 (hard multi-hop) against GPT-4's 73.58, 64.08, 34.40 and 23.01.
agent_test: Use the hard multi-hop items to test whether the scaffold helps multi-step situational reasoning.
audit_note: In SportQA Table 2 the human row (96.63/96.02/94.90/91.84) lines up under the four Level-3 columns (easy/hard single-hop, easy/hard multi-hop), not Levels 1-2; no human score is given for Levels 1-2, and human hard multi-hop is 91.84, not a single-hop figure. Only SportQA was read; the Sports Intelligence abstract was not opened.
claim_before_audit: LLMs are far below sport experts on text benchmarks of sport understanding: GPT-4 scores 85.63/78.82 on levels 1-2 against humans 96.63/96.02, and 23.01 on hard multi-hop against about 92-95 for human single-hop levels. Re-checked against the SportQA PDF.

claim: Reasoning before answering can hurt on perception-heavy sport tasks: Claude-3.5-Sonnet hard video 52.57% direct vs 39.32% rationale-first (SPORTU, re-checked); CoT effects in text are mixed (SportQA, Sports Intelligence) and a non-sport paper shows CoT drops on implicit tasks. Mind Your Step (Liu et al. 2024): CoT hurt on implicit statistical learning (GPT-4o 87.5 to 64.4), face recognition (GPT-4o 64.0 to 51.2) and exception learning (rounds 2.9 to 12.5); drops were smallest for Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Direct-then-check recovery is untested.
agent_test: Run direct-answer vs rationale-first vs answer-then-check at equal tokens on perception-like and rule-like items; report the sign per item type.
audit_note: SPORTU (52.57 to 39.32) and Mind Your Step numbers (87.5 to 64.4; 64.0 to 51.2; 2.9 to 12.5 rounds) match; 'smallest drops for Claude 3.5 Sonnet' fits (implicit learning -1.8 abs, i.e. no drop) though some small open models dropped less in absolute terms; the Sports Intelligence 'CoT mixed' point was not checked (abstract silent) and 'direct-then-check untested' is an absence claim.

claim: Strong LLMs are inconsistent across views of the same play: only 52.86% (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) of questions were correct at all camera angles; 28-39% mixed.
agent_test: Ask the same case in two paraphrases; measure agreement and use disagreement as a trigger to diagnose.

claim: No study found tests RPD directly in an LLM on athletes' decisions; the only close LLM tests are Kopka and Feufel (medical triage) and an unopened 2025 RPD-dynamics simulation. Bossard 2022 names zero AI studies. The 2025 Ivanova chapter is a finance chapter (Routledge, Decoding AI), unopened, so not a verified RPD test; a similarly surfaced 2026 geopolitical-simulation paper does not mention RPD.
agent_test: Build a small sport-decision set (text vignettes with expert-coded actions) and run the schema arms.
audit_note: Opened-status of the 2025 RPD-dynamics simulation and Ivanova chapter not checkable here; core facts (Bossard no AI, Kopka and Feufel numbers, Solopova no RPD mention) verified.

claim: Expert tactical AI with similar-case retrieval worked in one case: TacticAI (five Liverpool raters, 50 corners) was favoured over existing tactics 90% of the time; raters could not tell real from generated (F1 0.60); receiver top-3 0.782. Small panel, no outcome trial. Retrieval recall 0.63 vs 0.33 for a feature-cosine baseline (not vs no retrieval); no match-outcome trial.
agent_test: Check whether retrieving similar past cases (analogue of RPD match) improves the agent over no retrieval.

claim: Prompt structure strongly changes game-agent results: TextStarCraft II GPT-3.5 win rate at LV4 12.5% vs 84% with a different prompt; at LV5 0% vs 50%; the agent lost to pro and grandmaster humans (0/10 each).
agent_test: Ablate scaffold structure on a sequential game with a fixed token budget.

claim: LLMs reproduce some human decision biases (anchoring: GPT-3.5 low 20.83 vs high 105.97) and exceed humans on conjunction errors in a small sample (18 vs 10 of 20), so a recognition-first agent may inherit match errors.
agent_test: Add an anchor check at the first-match step and measure the shift.

claim: Research paradigm shapes what counts as evidence: of 53 reviewed studies 25 information processing, 18 ecological dynamics, 10 NDM, mostly decontextualised video tasks, so NDM usage rates are not comparable across paradigms.
agent_test: None direct; a caution when comparing sport findings with agent tasks.

claim: Within Kopka and Feufel, the RPD prompt's gain looks like a threshold shift toward lower-urgency advice: it came from self-care cases where the default was too cautious, not from better discrimination in nonemergency cases, and safety cannot be judged from 2 emergency cases.
agent_test: Report per-class accuracy and error direction when testing any NDM-style prompt; accuracy mean alone hides a shift.

claim: No test separates RPD content from extra reasoning text: Kopka's RPD and data-frame prompts performed alike (67.6 vs 66.7), neither was length matched, and the effect differs by model (8 of 10 gained).
agent_test: Four arms at equal tokens: neutral reasoning, recall only, simulate only, recall plus simulate.

claim: Reasoning-first hurts LLMs on tasks whose stimuli are implicit or hard to verbalise (statistical regularities, faces, exceptions), a plausible match to perception-heavy sport video; whether direct answer then check recovers accuracy is untested.
agent_test: For perception-like items answer directly first, then run a check step, and compare to reasoning-first on the same items.

claim: The option-count debate depends on what the rater scores: more options lift the best option but lower the mean quality of the set, expert option counts equal novices' but quality differs, and the positive count-quality link in soccer is correlational across players.
agent_test: Test option count while scoring first-option, best-of-set and chosen-option quality separately.
